objectives.wording: Calculate birth rate and maternal mortality ratio from sample data and distinguish morbidity and near miss.
Classify perinatal and neonatal outcomes and outline an audit of representative deaths and complications.
Compare definitions and apply applicable gestational thresholds in sample cases.
Assign representative births to modified Robson groups and interpret group contributions to the caesarean rate.
Explain indications, steps and complications of caesarean section.
Use official documents to map JSY, JSSK, SUMAN, Anaemia Mukt Bharat and vital registration to their purposes.
Relate tract development and pelvic organ relationships to obstetric and gynaecological procedures.
Sequence gametogenesis, ovulation, menstruation, fertilization and implantation.
Map embryonic development and explain how placental structure and maternal factors influence growth.
Recognize diabetes, hypertension, renal disease, lupus, obesity, epilepsy and cardiac disease in simulated cases and justify individualized care.
Identify antenatal risk factors and verify immunization status in a simulated record.
Demonstrate assessment of suspected pregnancy, consider alternatives and interpret representative pregnancy tests.
Compare pregnancy-related changes in the reproductive tract, breasts, circulation, respiration, blood, kidneys and gastrointestinal system.
Estimate gestational age, identify early risks and explain the inverted pyramid of care.
Demonstrate review of weight gain, fetal movement counts, nonstress testing and biophysical profile in simulation.
Justify initial and follow-up investigations, including ultrasound, based on gestation and clinical context.
Elicit, document and present menstrual, obstetric, medical and surgical history in simulation.
Demonstrate and document general and abdominal examination, including fundal height, abdominal girth and wellbeing assessment.
Demonstrate pelvic assessment on a model and explain how findings inform evaluation of cephalopelvic disproportion.
Assess a simulated diet and counsel on practical nutritional changes.
Use applicable guidance to compare vaccine types, indications and timing.
Classify possible causes and explain investigation, care and bereavement support.
Use operative history and current findings to compare birth options and monitoring needs.
Classify causes and justify investigations, counselling and management principles.
Compare ectopic pregnancy and other causes using clinical findings and investigations and explain medical and surgical management principles.
Integrate symptoms, hCG and ultrasound in representative cases and explain management and follow-up.
Explain mechanisms and maternal and fetal consequences and prioritize assessment and care.
Compare major causes, clinical and ultrasound findings and initial stabilization and management priorities.
Recognise antepartum haemorrhage and demonstrate initial stabilisation, teamwork and escalation in simulation.
Match blood components to representative indications and explain monitoring and management of complications.
Use chorionicity and clinical findings to explain investigations, complications and surveillance.
Classify hypertensive disorders and compare mechanisms, diagnostic findings, complications and management priorities.
Classify causes, interpret representative investigations and explain maternal and fetal effects and care through labour.
Distinguish pre-existing and gestational diabetes and explain testing, maternal and fetal risks and care through labour.
Compare representative causes and risk findings and explain investigations and management through labour.
Compare screening and diagnostic findings and explain how infection and pregnancy affect each other and guide care.
Distinguish pregnancy-specific from coincidental disease and compare presentation, investigations, risks and care.
Explain antenatal HIV screening and plan maternal and newborn care using applicable guidance.
Trace sensitization, prophylaxis and fetal complications and justify diagnostic and surveillance choices.
Compare mechanisms, prevention where applicable, testing, fetal risks and management.
Compare representative disorders and explain assessment, risk reduction and management adapted to pregnancy.
Differentiate suspected growth restriction from constitutional smallness and justify ultrasound, Doppler, surveillance, prevention and counselling.
Use serial growth, ultrasound and Doppler findings to justify monitoring and management and counsel on risk reduction.
Identify pelvic types and clinically relevant diameters on diagrams.
Demonstrate cardinal movements on a model.
Interpret labour charts and explain monitoring, analgesia, induction, augmentation and third-stage care.
Demonstrate the stages of normal labour on a mannequin.
Observe and assist with normal birth under supervision and record the role performed.
Explain the assessment and management of preterm labour.
Explain the assessment and management of prelabour rupture of membranes.
Explain the assessment and management of post-dated pregnancy.
Describe indications and precautions and document supervised observation or assistance.
Apply consent, dignity, privacy, communication and support to a simulated labour encounter.
Recognize findings and explain prevention, initial management and escalation.
Identify risk factors and signs and justify urgent escalation in simulation.
Compare occipitoposterior, breech, face and transverse presentations by recognition and management.
Compare indications, steps and complications of episiotomy, vacuum, forceps, assisted breech delivery and other operative obstetric procedures.
Document supervised observation and assigned assistance for outlet forceps, vacuum and breech delivery.
Demonstrate episiotomy repair on a model and document supervised observation or assistance across the specified operative births.
Demonstrate episiotomy and repair on a simulator using the approved skills checklist.
Classify causes, recognize haemorrhage and explain prevention, initial management and blood component use in simulation.
Demonstrate bimanual and aortic compression, balloon tamponade and anti-shock garment application in simulation.
Recognise postpartum haemorrhage and demonstrate initial stabilisation, teamwork and escalation in simulation.
Recognize inversion and explain causes, prevention and urgent management priorities.
Explain milk production and ejection and connect them to Baby-Friendly hospital practices.
Demonstrate positioning, attachment and breast care counselling with teach-back.
Compare findings and explain diagnostic and management pathways.
Assess simulated maturity and recognition of possible birth asphyxia and explain common newborn problems and resuscitation principles.
Integrate perinatal history and newborn findings and explain limits of individual indicators.
Demonstrate the steps using the approved neonatal resuscitation checklist.
Explain preparation, assessment, ventilation priorities and common difficulties.
Distinguish normal recovery from complications and explain assessment, management and contraceptive counselling.
Discuss reversible options and puerperal sterilization in simulation, respecting voluntary informed choice.
Compare temporary and permanent methods by suitability, technique, adverse effects and failure, including pills, male methods, emergency options and IUCDs.
Describe indications and major steps and document supervised observation or assistance.
Use applicable programme documents to map counselling, eligibility, delivery and follow-up.
Distinguish threatened, inevitable, incomplete, missed and septic abortion and explain management priorities.
Explain medical termination and electric or manual vacuum aspiration and document supervised observation or assistance.
Use applicable official law and guidance to compare trimester-specific indications, methods, complications and management.
Role-play informed consent for termination with attention to privacy, options and voluntariness.
Document supervised observation and assistance with first-trimester termination and evacuation for incomplete abortion.
Use the official PC-PNDT Act and amendments to explain applicable safeguards in a simulated case.
Explain indications and demonstrate insertion and removal on a simulator.
Demonstrate IUD insertion and removal on a model, including counselling and safety checks.
Recognize normal characteristics and variation across reproductive states.
Distinguish candidiasis, trichomoniasis and bacterial vaginosis and justify testing, hygiene counselling and syndromic or cause-directed management.
Compare normal puberty with abnormal patterns and explain management of representative problems.
Classify causes and justify investigations and management using a sample presentation.
Classify representative central and peripheral causes.
Compare primary and secondary causes and construct a staged investigation and management approach.
Classify causes and justify focused assessment, investigations and management.
Recognize representative injuries and explain risk reduction, assessment and care.
Recognize representative fistula presentations and explain causes, prevention and management.
Compare representative infections by mechanism, findings, tests and sequelae and apply a syndromic pathway to a simulated case.
Compare presentation and differential diagnoses and explain investigations, management and long-term implications.
Use a simulated case to link infection and inflammation to findings, differential diagnoses, testing, management and reproductive sequelae.
Assess both partners and explain when tubal assessment, ovulation induction or assisted reproduction is appropriate.
Compare methods for assessing tubal patency and explain when restoration may be considered.
Explain patient selection, monitoring and risks of ovulation induction.
Compare representative assisted reproductive techniques by purpose and indications.
Relate fibroid location to presentation, complications, differential diagnoses, investigations and management.
Evaluate a simulated presentation, exclude mimics and explain reproductive and metabolic management.
Enumerate the causes of hyperandrogenism and describe its investigation and management, distinguishing common presentations from those that need urgent workup.
Classify prolapse and relate risk factors, symptoms and examination to prevention and management.
Explain physiological changes and compare symptom management options, including individualized hormone therapy.
Classify causes and justify timely investigation and management in a simulated case.
Relate risk and pathology to presentation, differential diagnosis, investigations and staging.
Compare stage-based roles of surgery, radiation and systemic therapy.
Demonstrate a cervical screening workflow on a model, including consent, sampling and documentation.
Compare vaccination and screening approaches and explain the roles of VIA, VILI, cytology and colposcopy.
Compare eligibility, limitations and follow-up for cryotherapy, thermal ablation and excision.
Connect risk factors and pathology to symptoms, evaluation, staging and operative management.
Compare major tumour groups and use representative findings to justify evaluation, staging and management.
Classify representative conditions and integrate clinical, imaging and hCG findings into investigation, staging and follow-up.
Explain and demonstrate the key steps of D&C, endometrial aspiration with endocervical curettage and cervical biopsy on a model, and identify complications.
